text:
maria: PTAL at https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/482 — addressed review comments from last week. Summary: added unit test for the eviction edge, made the async-flush use jittered backoff (50–200ms), preserved metrics tags, and trimmed a noisy log. I left a short comment next to the jitter math.

dan: looking now. quick skim — i like the unit test direction. does the jitter change any latency SLOs?

maria: shouldn't. the flush path is only used under sustained cache pressure; in normal requests it's a no-op. added a note in the unit test and a brief changelog entry.

ekaterina: skimmed — one tiny nit: drop the noisy info log to debug so we don't spam prod traces. also can you add a comment explaining why we picked 50–200ms (collision avoidance with our batching window)?

maria: good call. changed the log to debug-only and added the comment explaining batching collision avoidance + reference to batching window. pushed commit 2f9a3c.

dan: unit test looks fine. left a single inline suggestion to rename a var for clarity, not a blocker.

maria: renamed var and force-pushed. ran tests locally, all green.

buildbot: CI passed — runtime-tests (14/14) — https://ci.example.com/builds/482/status

ekaterina: LGTM. any concerns about canary timing / merge slot?

alvin: no technical objections. ops: we can fit this in tomorrow's 09:00 UTC canary window unless capacity spikes. if there's high load we'll postpone.

maria: thanks — planning to request merge-ops in ~30m if no further comments. tagging for final eyes @dan @ekaterina

dan: approved :+1:

ekaterina: approved :shipit:

maria: thanks! scheduling the canary request and adding a short rollout note in the PR describing the metrics to watch (eviction rate, flush latency).

alvin: noted — i'll keep an eye on the metrics during canary. good job. :raised_hands:
